title: GridLock: choose the visual direction
question: The roll dealt The Plan Sheet, already raised by the six worlds it beat. Keep it, take Impeccable's pick or the category standard, adopt a declined world, or re-roll.

options.label: The Plan Sheet
options.lineage: Regional transmission plan project pages (SERTP 2025, DESC SCRTP 2026 to 2030)
options.thesis: Every opportunity filed like a page of the plans it came from: labelled fields, a folio, a citation you can open.
options.viewport: Full-bleed map captioned as the plan's figure; a docked summary table ranks the pairs with the top row highlighted; in-service years 2026 to 2035 run along the bottom edge as the slider.
options.risk: A document look can feel static on a live map; it only works if the panel stays a working tool, never a report to read.

raised.raise: Colour never touches chrome or text: the panel stays achromatic, and colour lives only on map lines, band rings and the one highlighter mark.
Every quantity is set like a tally board: tabular figures, right aligned, unit in a lighter weight, so km, kV, years and dollars scan as one column.
Approximate is pencil, exact is ink: a lighter dashed line and a lighter label wherever a location is approximate, in list, map and detail.
The selected pair and the top opportunities carry printed labels on hairline leaders, so the map never needs a legend lookup.
Distance bands carry a hatch density as well as a tint, so they survive grayscale, colour blindness and the printed report.
State prints itself: one status line reports every change as a plain sentence, for eyes and screen readers alike.

options.label: The System Wall Map
options.lineage: Utility transmission system maps on planning office walls
options.thesis: The wall map every planning office keeps, made live: line weight by voltage, colour by utility, the state line drawn heavy.
options.viewport: The SC and GA border full-bleed at wall-map scale; a docked panel drawn as the legend and title block holds search, filters and the ranked list.
options.risk: Where most tools in this category land: familiar and effective, and easy to mistake for any GIS viewer.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.lineage: Atmospheric optics: a cloud edge diffracting sunlight
options.thesis: An achromatic tool where colour appears only as a thin spectral fringe at each distance band's edge.
options.viewport: White map and panel; the 40 km, 8 km and 1.6 km rings drawn as mint, rose and violet hairlines around the selected pair.
options.case: Fuses with the band rings, but planners do not know this world and the pastel fringes carry little on a projector.
options.kept: The discipline: colour only on data, never on chrome or text.
options.risk: Pastel hairlines fail the 3:1 line contrast rule on a light basemap.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.lineage: Surreal worlds: a quarry cutting blocks of weather
options.thesis: Opportunities cut like blocks from a cloud cliff and stacked over deep blue gaps.
options.viewport: Panel sections stacked as cut blocks over blue gaps; the selected pair edged by one silver saw line.
options.case: Its tally boards carry numbers well; the surreal world tells a planner nothing about transmission.
options.kept: Quantities set like a tally board: tabular, right aligned, unit lighter.
options.risk: Reads as a game; a regulator would not trust it with a filing.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.thesis: Each pair as a folded J-card: side A one utility's project, side B the other's, years right aligned.
options.viewport: The pair detail opens as a J-card: side A the Dominion project, side B the Georgia project, in-service years right aligned.
options.case: Two hard halves fit a two-utility pair and pencil fits approximate data; handwriting costs trust and scan speed.
options.kept: Approximate is pencil, exact is ink, on every surface.
options.risk: Handwritten caps are slow to scan and read as a toy in front of a regulator.

options.label: Busytown Cross-Section
options.lineage: Picture-book publishing: the labelled cutaway spread
options.thesis: One continuous labelled scene where every project wears its printed name on a hairline pointer.
options.viewport: The border region as one labelled scene; opening a substation slices it away to show both utilities' work inside.
options.case: Direct labels make a map explain itself; the picture-book register undercuts a planner's trust.
options.kept: Printed labels on hairline leaders for the selected pair and top opportunities.
options.risk: Its red and green midtones collide for colour-blind viewers, and it reads as a children's book.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.lineage: Medium native: the early one-bit desktop
options.thesis: Map, list and pair as one-bit windows; bands as dither densities, selection as inversion.
options.viewport: Three windows (Map, Opportunities, Pair) on a dithered desktop; the 40 km circle wears marching ants.
options.case: Pattern coding is excellent for bands and print; pixel type and overlapping windows fail at 390 px.
options.kept: Bands hatched by density as well as tint, so they survive grayscale and print.
options.risk: Pixel type and stacked windows cost legibility and break the system font rule.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.lineage: Signals and instruments: the green-phosphor terminal
options.thesis: GridLock as a typed transcript: ask for a place and the ranked pairs print back.
options.viewport: A command line over a dark map: typing Savannah prints the ranked pairs as numbered lines.
options.case: Keyboard first and self-reporting state are right; green on black hides the map and is the dark dashboard rut.
options.kept: State prints itself: one status line reports every change as a plain sentence.
options.risk: Glow and monospace-only type break the system font rule and the light projector default.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean GIS web app played straight: neutral basemap, a left panel with search, filters and a ranked list.
canonCard.viewport: Map on the right; a white left panel with a search field, filter chips and ranked result rows.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every map tool; nothing on screen says two utilities' plans.
